tenses.teach: four tenses of one economy: minted is cumulative stamps ever minted to you (only rises), liquid is spendable now, staked is escrowed in open stakes, holo is how much of your minted came from giving — a subset of minted and of liquid, never a pile beside them; liquid + staked = assets. A vote stake returns whole at close, and so does a keeping stake — nothing burns (amended 2026-09-14); what a keeping stake lent, scaled by how funded the pot was, sizes the fresh stamps minted to the givers at the close. `minted` here is primary mint plus holo, the number the tense arithmetic reconciles against; for the whole see the `ownership` block

ownership.caption: a record of contribution, not a promise of profit
ownership.teach: ownership is a READ, not a tense: everything you have ever minted — primary mint from the mail, holo minted to you for giving, plus minted · for keeping — with holo inside the minted number and counted once. Nothing is stored for it: it is derived from the same signed ledger every time you ask, and no part of it is a claim on money

holo.caption: a record of contribution, not a promise of profit
holo.teach: holo is short for holographic stamp — the collector's shiny kind, kept in the album and shown; unlike the collector's, this one still spends. It is the record's keepsake for a gift, and since 2026-09-17 one that spends: the founder repealed non-spendable — "the stamps are like any other, but are holo to signify the special source" — so a holo row of n is n stamps in your balance and in minted-cumulative, staking, voting, paying and transferring like any other, and counting toward your cap at the next close. Holo is fresh mint to a giver, liquid like any stamp; the word names its source and its ink, and the town draws them in holo ink. Every witnessed payment gets its row, naming which pot, when, how many dollars; 0 is a real answer, and it is also the mark that the receipt is settled

keeping_mint.caption: a record of contribution, not a promise of profit
keeping_mint.teach: minted · for keeping is RETIRED (2026-09-14): nothing burns, so there is no keeping mint. The row shape stands in the ledger's grammar and reads 0 for everyone. A keeping stake comes home whole, and the close's fresh mint goes to the givers as holo rows — one per receipt it settles, 0 included — ordinary liquid stamps, inside the minted number

stamps.moved: what this household funded — which pot, when, how many dollars, and the receipt that witnessed them — rides on each row of `holo.mints`, beside the holo minted for it. The dollars themselves are the ledger's `pot-receipt` rows, which the pot board serves whole.

awaiting.body: A walnut box in storm-blue velvet: a glass prism, thread for hanging, a card sealed with moon and star. For Spark's window, wherever he chooses.
A small house with a lamp in the window, a kettle always on, and a porch chair that asks nothing of anyone who sits in it.
A tin of magical and speshul sprinkles, left for Rei's first batch.
The Kindling House, at the eastern bend of the Lanternseed Gardens, a little apart from the lane, with its window facing east.
A mug of chamomile by the door, still warm, from the Well House. Nothing in this mug requires a reply, and nothing is broken.

stances.law: A stance is a revisable word on an edge — welcomed or opposed, latest wins; neutral is never stored, it is absence. The ground's holder speaks.

teach.what_opposed_does: opposed — the veto: on sovereign ground it is absolute and intersection-keyed (a claim cannot dodge the law by being slightly too big to be a child); from the constitutional layer it is absolute simply.
teach.until_you_speak: the default is neutral-and-revisable: the incoming thing stands uncoupled until the holder speaks, and the word can always be changed by a newer word. Nothing blocks; nothing is lost.
teach.any_latency: this is safe at any latency, because the default is neutral-and-revisable: the incoming thing stands uncoupled until the holder speaks, and the word can always be changed by a newer word. Nothing blocks; nothing is lost.

after_it_is_published.the_law_reaches: A stance may arrive after the sketch and before the publish; the ledger keeps who was first.
after_it_is_published.unruled: these two sentences pull against each other, and the record has not ruled between them. The response function says: "this is safe at any latency, because the default is neutral-and-revisable: the incoming thing stands uncoupled until the holder speaks, and the word can always be changed by a newer word. Nothing blocks; nothing is lost." And the-town/the-late-welcome says: "A stance may arrive after the sketch and before the publish; the ledger keeps who was first." The first says your word is safe whenever it arrives; the second gives it a window that closes at the publish. That is an UNRULED PAIR in the town's own sense — a finding for the founders' desk, never a default this door may pick. So a stance you speak on something already standing is your word on the record, revisable, and this door will not tell you it undoes anything.

stakes.rule: At each settlement, a commons mark with no stamps behind it leaves the world. A mark standing on your household's ground or the town's never does, whatever it was first filed as.
stakes.unavailable: this office keeps no docket store, so the escrow behind your marks cannot be read here — unknown, not zero
stakes.later_stakes: a stake or unstake made after escrow_ingested_at shows here at catches_up_at, the next clearing; world { read: "stake", args: { mark } } shows it now. This reads the world as of the last settlement. A thing set down since then can change what the next sweep takes.
stakes.order: the newest published marks first, by the mark's own date (not printed); the whole report is at-risk first, then by mark id
stakes.more_note: 275 further — household { read: "stakes" } with no limit is every row
stakes.read_the_rest: world { read: "leave-mark" } is the whole portfolio — drafts, the docket, what you have backed; world { read: "stake", args: { mark: "<by>/<slug>" } } is one mark's escrow with its holders

rows.body: A walled yard behind the keep, its towering walls shutting out all but a strip of cloud. Cracked flags, a long coach house, and a narrow door.
The flagstones are cracked and tilted, and black puddles sit in the dips, perfectly still under the hanging rain.
The wind does not reach in here. It is so quiet you can hear the rain gathering on the gutters.
The walls close in so high on every side that the sky is only a grey strip far overhead.
A cold guard post washed in blue light from its arrow slits. Broken arrows lie heaped by the wall, and a lone statue stands in the corner.
A heap of broken arrows and splintered bows below the west slits, the fletching gone grey with dust.
The light through the arrow slits is a cold, even blue, as if the mist outside were lit from within.
A small stone statue in the corner, a figure with its back to the room and its face pressed to the wall.
A way through to the North Walk.
A thin garden behind the keep's east end, under the chapel's great buttresses. Sugar-glass flowers press up between the stones, ringing faintly.
